standard.title: Language reflects cultural practices, values and identity
standard.description: recognise that language reflects cultural practices, values and identity, and that this impacts on non-verbal and spoken communication
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify connections between the target language and cultural practices, and understand how language encodes values and identity (AC9LCH4U04). They can examine music, arts and cultural expression. They have not yet analysed how language variation across regional and community contexts encodes cultural identity, examined the impact of cultural language values on miscommunication, or reflected on their own intercultural positioning.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students recognise that language reflects cultural practices, values and identity — including how this shapes non-verbal and spoken communication, creates intercultural miscommunication, and connects to students' own experience as participants in two or more language communities.

nodes.label: Language choices and cultural values in communication
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how specific language choices in spoken and non-verbal communication reflect cultural practices and values, and explain the impact on interaction.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two examples of how language choices in the target language (verbal or non-verbal) reflect specific cultural values, and explain the impact on an interaction.
nodes.typical_width: Examine how language choices across contexts — address forms, politeness conventions, topic selection, non-verbal behaviour — reflect cultural values; discuss how the same interaction would be managed differently across cultural contexts; identify the interconnections between cultural practices and language use.
wider: Analyse a recorded or simulated intercultural interaction — identify the specific moments where cultural language values are visible and discuss how each shapes the interaction

Compare how a specific cultural value (e.g. respect for elders, directness, hospitality) is encoded in language and non-verbal behaviour differently in the target language community versus Australian English-speaking contexts
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding that language choices reflect cultural values is the conceptual prerequisite for all intercultural communication awareness. Students who cannot see the cultural logic behind language choices cannot identify miscommunication risks or develop the intercultural competence that this descriptor targets.

response_modes.reason: Cultural value encoding in language requires explicit analytical scaffolding — students need to move from observing a language choice to explaining the cultural logic behind it. Guided analysis with cultural context information builds this explanatory capacity before students can reason independently.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two examples of language choices reflecting cultural values
Explains the impact of at least one such choice on an interaction

nodes.label: Regional and community variation in language and culture
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how language varies across regions and communities within the target language world, and discuss what this variation reveals about cultural identity.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two regional or community language variations in the target language and explain what each reveals about identity or cultural context.
nodes.typical_width: Notice regional variation in language — dialects, community-specific vocabulary, language contact effects; identify culturally-specific additions that mark belonging to a region or community; explore how target language communities in Australia and overseas differ in their language practices.
wider: Research language variation in a specific target language region or diaspora community — identify specific language features that mark membership and discuss what they reveal about that community's history and identity

Compare how the target language is used in the local community with how it is used in a different regional or national community — identify specific differences and discuss what they reveal about cultural diversity within the target language world

response_modes.reason: Regional and community language variation is understood through exposure to varied examples. Students who have only encountered one variety of the target language will treat it as monolithic. Varied community encounters — including diaspora varieties, regional dialects, and community-specific practices — build the pluralistic understanding the descriptor requires.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background learners may speak a community variety of the target language that differs from standard forms. Width investment here — explicitly valuing and examining community varieties — validates students' own language knowledge and builds their confidence as target language speakers.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two regional or community language variations in the target language
Explains what at least one variation reveals about cultural identity or context

nodes.label: Intercultural positioning and personal reflection
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can reflect on their own experience of navigating between two or more language-culture communities, and identify how this shapes their communication and identity.
nodes.minimum_width: Reflect on at least one specific experience of navigating between two cultural-language contexts — identifying what felt different, what caused difficulty, or what new perspective emerged.
nodes.typical_width: Reflect on how interacting in the target language feels different from interacting in English; identify culturally-specific behaviours and communication styles; explore how students' multilingual experience shapes their perspective on cultural difference; discuss miscommunication experiences and what caused them.
wider: Describe a specific intercultural communication experience in depth — identifying the cultural values at play, what was assumed, what caused misunderstanding, and what was learned
Compare own intercultural navigation experience with that of a peer or community member — identify what is shared and what is specific to the student's own language history and community

response_modes.reason: Intercultural reflection integrates cultural value analysis (node 1) and community variation awareness (node 2) into a personally grounded synthesis. The teaching investment is in creating a reflective, non-judgmental environment where students can examine their own intercultural experiences honestly — including moments of discomfort or misalignment.

success_criteria: Reflects on at least one experience of navigating between two cultural-language contexts
Identifies at least one cultural value or communication difference that shaped that experience
